The voltages u1 and u2 are marked across Z1 and Z2 respectively. A voltmeter V is connected on a lower branch between the same left and right end nodes of the series combination, so it measures the total voltage across Z1 and Z2 together. Reasoning: The given instantaneous voltages are u1 = 80√2 sin(314t + 45°) V and u2 = 60√2 sin(314t - 45°) V. Converting to RMS phasors gives U1 = 80∠45° V and U2 = 60∠-45° V. The phase difference between U1 and U2 is 90°, so the RMS magnitude is |U| = √(80^2 + 60^2) = √10000 = 100 V.
